q-35021.name: Question 1
q-35021.problem: Express $\frac{\sqrt{x+1}}{\sqrt{x-1}}\,$ without radicals in the denominator.
q-35021.worked_solution:
To remove the radical $\sqrt{x-1}$ from the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{x-1}$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{x+1}}{\sqrt{x-1}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{x+1}}{\sqrt{x-1}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{x-1}}{\sqrt{x-1}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{x+1}\cdot \sqrt{x-1}}{(\sqrt{x-1})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{(x+1)(x-1)}}{x-1} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}{x-1}\end{aligned}
$$

q-35021.html:
Question 1
?

Express x+1x−1 without radicals in the denominator.

a
x−1x−1
b
x2+1x−1
c
x2+1x+1
d
x2−1x+1
e
x2−1x−1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To remove the radical x−1 from the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by x−1 and simplify:

x+1x−1=x+1x−1⋅x−1x−1=x+1⋅x−1(x−1)2=(x+1)(x−1)x−1=x2−1x−1

q-111056.name: Question 2
q-111056.worked_solution:
First, we apply the quotient rule and put the numerator and denominator under separate radicals:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{6}{7p}} & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{7p}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to remove the radical $\sqrt{7p}$ from the denominator. To do this, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{7p},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{7p}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{7p}}{\sqrt{7p}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{42p}}{(\sqrt{7p})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{42p}}{7p}\end{aligned}
$$

42p7p

EXPLANATION

q-111061.name: Question 3
q-111061.problem: Express $\sqrt{\frac{5}{a+b}}\,$ without radicals in the denominator.
q-111061.worked_solution:
First, we apply the quotient rule and put the numerator and denominator under separate radicals:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{5}{a+b}} & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{a+b}}\end{aligned}
$$

To remove the radical $\sqrt{a+b}$ from the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{a+b}$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{a+b}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{a+b}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{a+b}}{\sqrt{a+b}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{a+b}}{\sqrt{a+b}\cdot \sqrt{a+b}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5(a+b)}}{(\sqrt{a+b})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5(a+b)}}{a+b} & \end{aligned}
$$

q-111061.html:
Question 3
?

Express 5a+b without radicals in the denominator.

a
5(a+b)
b
 5(a+b)5(a+b)
c
5a+ba+b
d
5(a+b)a+b
e
a+b5(a+b)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we apply the quotient rule and put the numerator and denominator under separate radicals: 5a+b=5a+b

To remove the radical a+b from the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by a+b and simplify:

5a+b=5a+b⋅a+ba+b=5⋅a+ba+b⋅a+b=5(a+b)(a+b)2=5(a+b)a+b
